statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the number of sequences (r_0,c_0),...,(r_{K-1},c_{K-1}) such that: (1) (r_0,c_0) = (sr,sc) and (r_{K-1},c_{K-1}) = (er,ec); (2) for every t with 0 <= t < K, 0 <= r_t < m, 0 <= c_t < n, and grid[r_t][c_t] != -1; (3) for every t with 0 <= t < K-1, |r_{t+1}-r_t| + |c_{t+1}-c_t| = 1; (4) for every non-obstacle cell (i,j), there is exactly one t with (r_t,c_t) = (i,j). In other words, r is the number of 4-directional walks from the start to the end that visit every non-obstacle cell exactly once.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 (the start) and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2 (the end). A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells (so K >= 2).

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail: no panic, out-of-bounds access, or 64-bit overflow) for every grid satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= (K-2)! (ordinary factorial; K >= 2). Equivalently, r is non-negative and is at most the number of permutations of the K-2 non-obstacle cells other than the start and end.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells.

statement: The function returns r, and r = 1 if |sr-er| + |sc-ec| = 1 (the start and end are 4-adjacent), and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells. In addition, K = 2, so the only non-obstacle cells are the start and the end.

statement: The function returns r, and r = 1 if |sr-ur| + |sc-uc| = 1 and |er-ur| + |ec-uc| = 1, and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells. In addition, K = 3; let (ur,uc) be the unique non-obstacle cell that is neither the start nor the end (so grid[ur][uc] = 0).

statement: The function returns r, and r = 1 if S = {c | a <= c <= b} and {sc,ec} = {a,b}; otherwise r = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells. In addition, m = 1. Let S = {c | 0 <= c < n and grid[0][c] != -1}, let a = min S, and let b = max S. The start column is sc and the end column is ec (both rows are 0).

statement: The function returns r, and r = 1 if S = {i | a <= i <= b} and {sr,er} = {a,b}; otherwise r = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells. In addition, n = 1. Let S = {i | 0 <= i < m and grid[i][0] != -1}, let a = min S, and let b = max S. The start row is sr and the end row is er (both columns are 0).

statement: If either (K is even and (sr+sc) mod 2 = (er+ec) mod 2) or (K is odd and (sr+sc) mod 2 != (er+ec) mod 2), then the function returns r with r = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, m*n <= 20; every row grid[i] has length n; every entry grid[i][j] is one of -1, 0, 1, 2; there is exactly one cell (sr,sc) with grid[sr][sc] = 1 and exactly one cell (er,ec) with grid[er][ec] = 2. A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells.

statement: Let G be the undirected graph whose vertices are the non-obstacle cells, with an edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding cells are 4-adjacent. If G is not connected, then the function returns r with r = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). A non-obstacle cell is any (i,j) with grid[i][j] != -1; let K be the number of non-obstacle cells.

statement: Let G be the graph on non-obstacle cells with 4-adjacency edges. If G has a non-obstacle cell that is neither the start nor the end and has degree less than 2, or has the start or the end with degree less than 1, then the function returns r with r = 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). statement: Let grid' be the grid obtained from grid by replacing every 1 by 2 and every 2 by 1 (all other entries unchanged). Let r be the result of the function on grid and r' the result on grid'. Then the function returns both results and r = r'.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). statement: Let grid^T be the n by m transpose of grid, defined by grid^T[j][i] = grid[i][j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Let r and r' be the results of the function on grid and grid^T respectively. Then r = r'.

statement: Let G be the undirected graph whose vertices are the non-obstacle cells, with an edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding cells are 4-adjacent. For a non-obstacle cell v, let c(v) be the number of connected components of the graph obtained from G by deleting v and all its incident edges (on the remaining non-obstacle cells). If v is the start or the end and c(v) > 1, or v is neither the start nor the end and c(v) > 2, then the function returns a result r with r = 0.
